title: Common School: venial stain in the damned persists forever—no repentance there
source_text: XXI. Sed communis Scholae Romanae sententia contrarium tenet, scilicet, poenam peccati venialis in damnatis fore perpetuam. Idque quoniam peccatum quodvis quantumlibet leve, hominem supplicio & poena dignum reddit, quamdiu in eo manet, & nisi per poenitentiam aliquam retractatum & expiatum non est. Jam autem in damnatis nulla datur poenitentia, & peccati expiatio: adeoque in iis perpetuae manent maculae ex peccatis etiam venialibus contractae. Nec enim ullum omnino peccatum per aliquem dilectionis, sive contritionis actum retractare possunt: quoniam ista locum in inferno non habent. Et sic cum peccati venialis macula & pravitas aeternum in iis perseveret, in aeternum quoque per eam supplicio & poena digni manent.
pass_a_gloss: But the common opinion of the Roman School holds the contrary, namely, that the punishment of venial sin in the damned will be perpetual. And that because any sin, however light, renders a person worthy of torment and punishment so long as it remains in him and has not been retracted and expiated by some repentance. But now in the damned no repentance and expiation of sin is given: and so in them the stains contracted even from venial sins remain perpetual. For they can retract no sin at all by any act of love or contrition, because those have no place in hell. And thus since the stain and wickedness of venial sin perseveres forever in them, through it they also forever remain worthy of torment and punishment.
pass_b_english: Against Scotus, the common line keeps venial punishment perpetual in the damned—no repentance can clear the stain there.
While the stain remains, even light fault keeps them worthy of endless penalty.

choices.why: Moral blemish that grounds ongoing desert of penalty.
